title: Flatten Once
statement: Implement `solve(rows)`. `rows` is a list of lists of integers. Return one list with each inner list's items in order. Do not flatten any deeper: the inputs are exactly one level. An empty outer list or empty inner lists contribute nothing.
hints: A double iteration, outer row then item, is the whole algorithm.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: One-level flatten is a nested loop, which a comprehension writes in one expression.

editorial: One-level flatten is a nested loop, which a comprehension writes in one expression. Recursion would matter for irregular trees. These rows are rectangular in depth, so the extra machinery can only hide an off-by-one level.
reference_solution:
def solve(rows):
    return [item for row in rows for item in row]
